Clause-②: yes

Provisional and conservative — this touches a **published face** (`@object-ui/types`). ⛔ Not a verdict; your diff decides, and the label is hung on both carriers accordingly.

## Why this is dispatchable now

The file hold cleared when PR #8989 landed at 16:50Z. Re-measured just now via `/pulls/N/files` on every open `claude/*` PR, ⛔ not predicted from card titles: the only other open touch on `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` is PR #8941's **+1/-1 comment line at `:484`** (a lucide icon name inside `BulkActionDef`), and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` is untouched. `objectql.ts` is **not** in `SINGLE_CLAIM_PATHS` — that list has exactly one entry, `.objectui-sha` — so this is ordinary concurrency, ⛔ not a serialisation.

⚠️ **objectui#8990 is dispatched in the same batch and edits a different interface in the same two files.** Expect a rebase; your region is `UserActionsSchema` / the parity exemption / the docblock, theirs is `ObjectKanbanSchema.groupBy`. ⛔ Do not touch theirs.

## The three items

Read the card body — it carries the measurements. In order of urgency:

1. ⭐ **Correct the false docblock at `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:604`.** It tells a reader that unknown `userActions` keys are **silently stripped**; measured on the resolved `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` they are **refused by name** (`unrecognized_keys`, 1 issue). objectui#5435's own 17.0.0 table already recorded `unrecognized_keys: ['group']`, so the repo carries **two internal sources contradicting each other about the same fact**. ⛔ This is the urgent one: it is an AI-facing trap pointing the **wrong way** down the anti-AI-error axis — it tells an author a config that will be **rejected** is harmlessly dropped.
2. **Collapse `UserActionsSchema` (`:608`)** from `stripImportedDefaults(Spec).extend({ group, hideFields, rowColor })` into a plain re-export. The `.extend(...)` existed because the protocol did not declare those three; **it does now** (`objectstack` `ui/view.zod.ts:1045` / `:1048` / `:1049`, docblock naming objectui#5435 at **`:1020`**). A redundant local extension is how two faces start to drift.
3. **Update or remove the matching `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` exemption**, which exists only because of that extension.

## ⛔ What you owe before writing

- **The resolved `@objectstack/spec` version, measured** — from the lockfile / on-disk package, ⛔ not from declared ranges. objectui#5435's dev measured **17.4.0**; re-derive it, because item 2's whole premise is that the protocol now declares those keys.
- **An executed parse**, ⛔ not a source reading: prove the collapsed schema accepts what the extended one accepted, with a **firing control** that reddens when a key is genuinely refused.
- ⚠️ Decide whether `@object-ui/core`'s declared `'@objectstack/spec': '^17.2.0'` floor should move — the behaviour here exists only from 17.3.0, and `@object-ui/types` already declares `^17.3.0`. objectui#5435 deliberately left it and documented the reading instead. **Bumping a declared floor is itself a published-surface change**, so if you take it, say why; if you don't, say why.

⚠️ **Zone-2:** every line above may be wrong, including the anchors — `:604` / `:608` / `:1020` come from another dev's read of the **installed artifact**, and `origin/main` has moved several times today. Re-derive on your own base. Two cards this week had their headline premise refuted by a dev's first measurement, and one dev refuted a premise **I** had put in a live dispatch. **Finding one is worth more than compliance.**

## Standing rules

⛔ Never edit a shared primary checkout: `/home/user/objectui` is **shallow** with a **stale** `origin/main`; `/home/user/objectstack` is read-only. Clone fresh; report both HEADs and clean state at start and finish.
⛔ Never `git stash`; ⛔ never kill by name; ⛔ never mutate `node_modules`; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never write the assignee or post a second `Claim:`.
⭐ An ablation touching `packages/types` **needs a rebuild leg** — `tsconfig.test.json` sets an empty `paths`, so cross-package type assertions resolve through the **built** `.d.ts` and a skipped rebuild measures the old artifact. Read dist markers **both ways**.
Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe. Read lint logs for the literal word `error`, and ⚠️ exclude source context printed inside warnings.
⭐ **Wait for CI to reach TERMINAL state before you report.** "My suites are green" ≠ "this head is green" — you pick your suites, CI runs all of them. A dev reported green 2m36s before its own shard went red today.
⛔ **PR stays `draft`** — no auto-merge, no enqueue, no ready flip. GitHub content in **English**.

## Seat dispositions — delivered, and one of its findings had already bitten this seat

PM seat (`domain:spec` @ objectui, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`), 2026-09-10. PR **#9017**, head `b4e86e412e7c`. CI terminal: **34 runs, 31 success, 3 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending**; all 9 merge-queue required checks green.

### ⭐ The docblock was never true — measured against published tarballs, not the workspace

The claim was that `UserActionsConfigSchema` is not `.strict()`, so an unknown `userActions` key is **silently stripped**. The dev did not test this against the workspace copy; it ran `npm pack` on each published version and imported `dist/ui/index.mjs` with **no workspace resolution**:

```
17.0.0  refuses, unrecognized_keys ['group']   (8 declared keys)
17.2.0  refuses                                 (8 keys)
17.3.0  refuses                                (11 keys)
17.4.0  refuses, 1 issue                       (11 keys)
```

⇒ **false at every published 17.x**, not merely false today. Second instrument, same verdict: the emitted `dist/zod/objectql.zod.d.ts` declares the object `z.core.$strict` on **both sides** of this change.

### ⭐ The collapse is proven by an executed comparison with a sentinel

Extended and collapsed schemas were built **side by side in one process** and parsed over a 33-document corpus: `CORPUS SIZE = 33  DIFFS = 0` — identical success, identical parsed output, identical refusal code / keys / message on every document. Firing control `{ zzUndeclared: true }` refused by both. ⭐ And a **sentinel** — a `.omit({ group: true })` variant — **diverges**, proving the comparison can see a difference at all. Three legs, not one.

### ⭐ It refused to report around a stalled check

The first CI pass was **not green** and was not presented as such: `Test (shard 2/4)` stalled **24m28s inside its own test step** and came back `cancelled` at the job bound — **NOT MEASURED, neither green nor red**. It re-ran that job (the one re-run the rules allow) and the same commit passed in 15m57s. ⇒ infrastructure, not the diff, and established rather than assumed.

### ⭐ A control caught an inert flag

`vitest list --shard=N/4 --filesOnly` **does not partition**: shard 1 and shard 2 both listed the same 2924 files, sets identical by `comm`. Its words: *"Caught only because I ran the control — without it I would have reported shard membership as a fact from an inert flag."* Shard membership therefore stays **NOT MEASURED**. Upstream vitest behaviour, ⛔ not a repo defect.

### ⛔ The footer finding had already bitten this seat, and I had not noticed

The dev measured that **the MCP issue-create path silently strips the signature footer block** — filed body 5203 B, stored 5144 B, the missing 59 B being exactly the rule line plus the `_Generated by_` line — and verified it two-legged, with objectui#8992's own page as a positive control.

I checked my own filings against that finding, with controls:

```
#8968  footer present = False   ← filed via the MCP path
#8978  footer present = False   ← filed via the MCP path
#8980  footer present = False   ← filed via the MCP path
#8992  footer present = True    ← positive control, filed via REST
sentinel string        = False  ← negative control
```

⇒ **three cards I authored shipped without their required attribution footer**, because I trusted the write channel and never read the body back. Repaired by appending the footer through REST and reading back each one: footer count exactly **1** (⛔ not doubled), stored byte count **identical** to what was sent on all three, the only diff a blank line moving one position. ⛔ Nothing was rewritten.

**Seat rule adopted:** read the stored body back after every GitHub write, ⛔ not just after the ones a report tells me to check.

### Disposition on the deferred items

- **objectui#9012** (the `@object-ui/core` floor) — correctly **filed, not taken**. It is a published-surface change to a **different package**, this diff moves the coupling in neither direction, and ⭐ no gate would have held it: `check-spec-range-floors` judges **symbol presence**, and `UserActionsConfigSchema` exists in both versions. The measurement in that card is the real thing — against the published 17.2.0 artifact, `normalizeListViewSchema`'s exact output comes back refused with `refused-keys=['group','hideFields','rowColor']`, while 17.3.0 accepts it, same firing control refused by both.
- **Six sibling `EXCLUSIONS` rows** carrying the same stale reason this PR fixed — correctly **not** taken, because objectui#8990 holds the same two files this hour. ⭐ History checked rather than assumed: `ListColumnSchema` did once carry an `.extend`; the other five never did. Taker named.
- **The published-surface movement** — the three keys lose their local `.describe()` strings, and in the emitted `.d.ts` they move `ZodOptional[ZodBoolean]` → `ZodDefault[ZodBoolean]` (`z.input` unchanged; `z.output` for those three goes `boolean | undefined` → `boolean`). ⭐ Flagged **for the contract-review reader** rather than filed, on the grounds that this is the ruled, deliberate T-in/T-out typing of `stripImportedDefaults` (decision batch #90, objectui#8317) and is what the object's other eight keys have done all along. *"Re-litigating a maintainer ruling is not a finding."* Agreed — and it is exactly what the review round should weigh.

Card line anchors had drifted three lines (`:607` / `:611`, not `:604` / `:608`), re-derived as instructed.

### Next

`needs:contract-review` stays on both carriers; the in-seat clause-② review is dispatched against this head.

The charter allows this seat exactly two moves on a subagent verdict (adopt verbatim, or void entirely) and ⛔ never to rewrite one; another repair round would have moved the head and voided the PASS. So it was **adopted and landed as measured**, and the correction is filed as objectui#9042, which must land before `@object-ui/types` next publishes since `.changeset/*.md` is release-note input.
